concepts.name: The LORD on His throne
concepts.why: Biblical-theological / secular academic: the name says 'in heaven', but Psalm 93:2, Psalm 99:1 (above the cherubim), Isaiah 6:1 (in the temple) and Lamentations 5:19 do not say heaven; Isaiah 6:1 is expressly a temple vision. The name says more than four of its eight passages. A plain label that all eight hold is safe; Psalm 103:19, Psalm 11:4, Isaiah 66:1 and Revelation 4:2 still carry heaven in their own notes. All notes are exact quotations.

concepts.name: The Most High rules over the kingdom of mankind
concepts.why: Secular academic / biblical-theological: 'gives them to whom He wishes' is said only in Daniel 4:17 and 5:21; 1 Chronicles 29, Psalm 22:28, Psalm 47:8 and Daniel 4:34-35 say that He rules or does as He pleases, not that He gives kingdoms away. The Daniel 4:17 / 5:21 wording ('rules over the kingdom of mankind') is held by every passage here (2 Chronicles 20:6 'kingdoms of the nations', Daniel 2:21 'removes kings and establishes them'). Notes are exact.

concepts.name: Kingdoms that will arise from the earth
concepts.why: Secular academic / Reformed / Baptist-dispensational: 'These four great beasts are four kings' is Daniel 7:17 only. Daniel 2 has a statue, not beasts, and Daniel 8:20-21 is a ram and a goat (two kings), so the name says more than four of the six passages. Worse, putting Daniel 8:20-21 under a four-kingdom name reads as mapping Media-Persia and Greece onto the four, which is exactly where the academic reading (Babylon, Media, Persia, Greece) and the traditional one (ending in Rome) part. A plain label with no number takes no side on the four; Daniel 7:17 and 7:23 keep the beasts in their own notes. Keep every passage; all notes are exact.

Secular academic / Jewish reader of the Hebrew: in Deuteronomy 33:5 the Hebrew says only 'he was king in Jeshurun' with no named subject; 'the LORD' is the translator's supply, and Moses is read as the king by many. Under 'the original arbitrates', the note rests on the translation's reading and goes unless MACULA names the subject. The other seven passages say it in their own words.

Biblical-theological / secular academic: the name is about ruling in the fear of God. Deuteronomy 17:15 and 1 Samuel 16:1 are about who chooses the king, not how he rules, and Psalm 72:1-2 asks for justice and righteousness (it already stands in concept 14). Deuteronomy 17:18-20, 1 Samuel 12:14 and 2 Samuel 23:3-4 hold the name. The dropped choosing passages are not lost: see missing 'The king whom the LORD your God shall choose'. 1 Samuel 16:1 also stays in section C.

concepts.name: The kingdom taken away from you
concepts.why: Secular academic / biblical-theological: 'torn' is said only in 1 Samuel and 1 Kings, and 'given to another' is not in Daniel 4:31 ('has departed from you'). 'Taken away from you' is held by all seven (1 Samuel 15:28 and 1 Kings 11:11 'from you', Daniel 4:31, Matthew 21:43 'taken away from you'); the notes then show the 'given' half where the verse says it. Israel and the church: Matthew 21:43 is kept as the verse's own words, last in a run of kings who lost kingdoms, with no word of replacement or fulfilment in the name; do not add one.

Biblical-theological / secular academic: 1 Corinthians 15:25 echoes the footstool clause but has no 'right hand' and no 'sit'; it holds a word, not the concept. It is not lost, since 1 Corinthians 15:28 already stands in concept 25 and 15:25 can go there instead. The NT passages that quote or say Psalm 110:1 in their own words are correct to keep, with no fulfilment claim in the name. Acts 2:34-35 and Hebrews 1:13 correctly carry no note.

concepts.name: Proclaiming the kingdom of God
concepts.why: Secular academic / Lutheran: 'gospel of the kingdom' is said in Matthew 4:23, 9:35, 24:14 and (as 'gospel of the kingdom of God') Acts 8:12, and as 'good news' in Luke 4:43 and 8:1, but Acts 1:3 ('spoke about the kingdom of God') and Acts 28:31 ('proclaimed the kingdom of God') do not say gospel. Acts 28:31's word 'proclaimed' is held by all eight. Notes are exact.

Baptist-dispensational / Reformed / secular academic: Colossians 1:13 says believers were 'brought into the kingdom', not that the kingdom 'has come upon you'; it shares the word kingdom and nothing more. It fits concept 21 (Enter the kingdom) and should move there. Luke 17:20-21 'is in your midst' is acceptable under the name, and its note is exactly the BSB (the Greek 'within/among' is not decided here, which is right).

concepts.name: Your kingdom come; seek His kingdom
concepts.why: Biblical-theological: Matthew 6:33 and Luke 12:31 say seek the kingdom, not 'Your kingdom come', so half the passages do not hold the name. Naming both texts' words keeps all four. Notes are exact. The name takes no side on whether the coming is present or future.

secondary_or_links: Authority -> in heaven and on earth: Daniel 7:14 says dominion was given, not 'in heaven and on earth' (that is Matthew 28:18's wording). Rename the line 'Authority -> given to Him' (both verses say it was given); the label as it stands says more than Daniel 7:14 and, set beside a New Testament verse, reads as saying one answers the other.

Kingdom -> divided against itself: drop Daniel 5:28 (a kingdom divided and given to the Medes and Persians is not a kingdom divided against itself); it already stands in concept 10. Keep Matthew 12:25 and Mark 3:24; Luke 11:17 may be added.
Colossians 1:13 (dropped from concept 17) belongs under concept 21, Enter the kingdom, with its own note 'brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son'.
1 Corinthians 15:25 (dropped from concept 13) may be placed in concept 25 beside 15:28; it says 'He must reign', in the texts' words.
Links: no change. The nine are held by the passages (Spirit by Matthew 12:28 and Romans 14:17; Image of God by Genesis 1:26-28 in section C).

Last concept (25): checked. It is the texts' words from inside the theme (Revelation 11:15, Daniel 7:18 and 7:27, Zechariah 14:9, Luke 12:32, 1 Corinthians 15:28, Revelation 22:3-5), and nothing dark was dropped to make room: the hard words stand in concepts 10, 21 and 23 and Matthew 8:12 is kept in section C. The one dark half missing anywhere is Matthew 25:41 beside 25:34, left to the Judgment link and not required here.

missing.sub_theme: Are You the king of the Jews?
missing.why: The Gospels develop Jesus as king (the Magi's question, Pilate's question and 'You say that I am a king', the crowd's 'the King who comes in the name of the Lord') and a reader of this theme expects it; the outline reaches it only through Zechariah 9:9 / Matthew 21:5 and Luke 1:32-33. Titles and questions in the texts' words, no more.

missing.sub_theme: The king whom the LORD your God shall choose
missing.why: Who chooses the king is a thread the texts plainly run (Deuteronomy 17:15, 1 Samuel 16:1, Psalm 78:70 'He chose David His servant'); it is also where the passages dropped from concept 9 belong, and it stands apart from how the king must rule.

missing.sub_theme: This is what the king who will reign over you will do
missing.why: The hard side of human kingship: Samuel's warning ('he will take'), the years with no king, and Jotham's fable. The outline has 1 Samuel 8:7 only, inside 'The LORD your King'; without these the kingship material is all favourable.

The texts set the kings of the earth against, and bowing to, the LORD's king ('The kings of the earth take their stand', 'May all kings bow down to him', 'the kings of the earth and their armies'). It is a plain label with no order of the last things in it; omitting the kings who resist leaves the reign with no opposition anywhere in the outline.
